questionTextEn: Which article of the Indian Constitution describes India as a "Union of States"?
explanationEn: Article 1 of the Constitution states that "India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States." The term "Union" was preferred over "Federation."
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: In which of the following cases can the Union Parliament legislate on subjects in the State List?
explanationEn: The Constitution allows Parliament to legislate on State subjects under several circumstances: Emergency (Art 250), Rajya Sabha resolution (Art 249), international treaties (Art 253), and request by states (Art 252).
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Residuary powers in India are vested in:
explanationEn: Unlike the US where residuary powers rest with States, Article 248 of the Indian Constitution vests them exclusively in the Union Parliament.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The Sarkaria Commission (1983) was primarily concerned with:
explanationEn: The Sarkaria Commission was appointed in 1983 to examine the relationship and balance of power between the Centre and the States.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution is considered "Unitary" in nature?
explanationEn: Single Citizenship and All-India Services are unitary features. Written Constitution and Independent Judiciary are federal features.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The power of the Parliament to alter the boundaries or change the name of any State under Article 3 is:
optionAEn: Dependent on the consent of the concerned State legislature
optionBEn: Subject to a special majority in Parliament
optionCEn: Independent of the consent of the concerned State legislature
explanationEn: While the President must refer the bill to the State legislature for views, the views are not binding on the Parliament.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Inter-State Water Disputes are resolved by:
optionAEn: The Supreme Court under its Original Jurisdiction
explanationEn: Article 262 empowers Parliament to provide for the adjudication of disputes relating to waters of inter-state rivers/valleys. Parliament has excluded the jurisdiction of courts in such matters via the Inter-State Water Disputes Act.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
optionCEn: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
explanationEn: Under Article 64, the Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: A Money Bill can be introduced in:
explanationEn: Per Article 109, a Money Bill (defined in Art 110) cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha; it must originate in the Lok Sabha.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: What is the maximum period within which the Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill to the Lok Sabha?
explanationEn: After a Money Bill is passed by the Lok Sabha, the Rajya Sabha has only 14 days to recommend changes or approve it.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Who presides over a Joint Sitting of the Parliament?
optionCEn: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
explanationEn: Article 118(4) specifies that the Speaker of the Lok Sabha (or in their absence, the Deputy Speaker) presides over joint sittings.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Which House of Parliament can alone initiate the procedure for the removal of the Vice-President?
explanationEn: The Vice-President can be removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by an effective majority and agreed to by the Lok Sabha.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The 'No-Confidence Motion' against the Council of Ministers can be moved only in:
explanationEn: Since the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (Article 75), the motion of no-confidence can only be moved in the Lok Sabha.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Which of the following are the exclusive powers of the Rajya Sabha?
explanationEn: Articles 249 (State List) and 312 (All-India Services) are special powers exclusive to the Rajya Sabha.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The concept of 'Judicial Review' in India is based on:
explanationEn: While the concept has evolved significantly, the Indian Constitution specifically uses the phrase "procedure established by law" (Art 21), though the SC has moved closer to "due process" since the Maneka Gandhi case.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Which article of the Constitution declares all laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights to be void?
explanationEn: Article 13 provides the constitutional basis for judicial review by declaring that any law in force that is inconsistent with FRs shall be void.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Public Interest Litigation (PIL) was pioneered in India by:
explanationEn: Justice P.N. Bhagwati and Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer are considered the pioneers of PIL in India (Sunil Batra case, Hussainara Khatoon case).
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: A person can move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights under:
explanationEn: Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) allows citizens to approach the Supreme Court directly for FR enforcement. Dr. Ambedkar called it the "Heart and Soul" of the Constitution.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The 'Doctrine of Basic Structure' was first propounded by the Supreme Court in the:
explanationEn: In the landmark Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), the SC ruled that Article 368 does not enable Parliament to alter the 'basic structure' of the Constitution.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Judicial Review power of the High Courts is wider than that of the Supreme Court because:
optionAEn: High Courts can review State laws only
optionBEn: High Courts can issue writs for purposes other than Fundamental Rights
optionDEn: Supreme Court is an appellate court only
explanationEn: Under Article 226, HCs can issue writs for the enforcement of FRs *and* for "any other purpose," whereas the SC's writ jurisdiction under Art 32 is limited to FR enforcement.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Which article empowers the Supreme Court to review any judgment pronounced or order made by it?
explanationEn: Article 137 gives the SC the power to review its own judgments to rectify errors.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with the privileges of the State Legislature?
explanationEn: Article 194 defines the powers, privileges, and immunities of State Legislatures and their members (comparable to Art 105 for Parliament).
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: A member of the State Legislature cannot be arrested in a civil case:
optionBEn: During the session of the House only
optionCEn: During the session and 40 days before and after the session
optionDEn: Only when inside the House premises
explanationEn: This is an individual privilege to ensure members can attend sessions without interference in civil matters.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: No member of the State Legislature is liable to any proceedings in any court in respect of anything said in the House. This is called:
optionBEn: Freedom of speech in the House
explanationEn: Article 194(1) guarantees freedom of speech in the legislature, and 194(2) provides immunity from court proceedings for such speech.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Who has the power to punish a person for "Breach of Privilege" or "Contempt of the House"?
explanationEn: Each House has the inherent power to protect its dignity and punish any person (member or outsider) for breach of privilege.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Which of the following is NOT a collective privilege of the State Legislature?
optionAEn: Right to exclude strangers from proceedings
optionBEn: Right to publish reports and prohibit others from doing so
optionCEn: Right to be exempted from serving as a juror
optionDEn: Right to regulate its own internal procedure
explanationEn: Exemption from jury service is an *individual* privilege of a member, not a collective privilege of the House.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Can the privileges of the State Legislature be codified by a law?
optionBEn: No, they are fixed by the Constitution
optionDEn: Only with the President's prior permission
explanationEn: Article 194(3) allows the State Legislature to define its privileges by law. Until then, they remain the same as those of the UK House of Commons as of 1950.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The freedom of speech of a member in the State Legislature is:
optionAEn: Absolute and not subject to any restriction
optionBEn: Subject only to the provisions of the Constitution and the rules of the House
optionCEn: Same as the general freedom of speech under Article 19(1)(a)
optionDEn: Subject to the prior approval of the Governor
explanationEn: While broader than Art 19(1)(a), it is still subject to constitutional provisions (like Art 211 - restriction on discussing conduct of judges) and the Speaker's rules of procedure.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The 11th Schedule of the Constitution, added by the 73rd Amendment, contains:
explanationEn: The 11th Schedule lists 29 functional items that may be transferred to Panchayati Raj Institutions.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: What is the minimum age prescribed for contesting elections to a Panchayat?
explanationEn: Article 243-F states that a person is qualified to be a member of a Panchayat if they have attained the age of 21 years.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Which of the following is the "Gram Sabha"?
optionAEn: All adult residents of the village
optionBEn: All persons whose names are registered in the electoral rolls of the village
optionCEn: The elected members of the Panchayat
explanationEn: Article 243(b) defines Gram Sabha as a body consisting of persons registered in the electoral rolls relating to a village comprised within the area of Panchayat at the village level.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The State Finance Commission is appointed by:
explanationEn: Under Article 243-I, the Governor of a State appoints a Finance Commission every five years to review the financial position of local bodies.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Reservation of seats for SCs and STs in Panchayats is:
optionAEn: Compulsory and based on their proportion in total population
optionBEn: Discretionary and at the will of the State Government
optionCEn: Limited to the village level only
explanationEn: Article 243-D makes reservation of seats for SCs/STs mandatory in every Panchayat in proportion to their population.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: The 'Nagarpalikas' (Municipalities) were given constitutional status by which amendment?
explanationEn: The 74th Amendment Act of 1992 (effective 1993) provided constitutional status to urban local bodies.
subject: Polity

questionTextEn: Who is responsible for the delimitation of constituencies and the conduct of elections for Panchayats?
explanationEn: The State Election Commission (Article 243-K) is solely responsible for the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of all elections to the Panchayats.
subject: Polity
